transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Tom Richards (CISO), Nina Gomez (Head of Cloud Ops), Raj Banerjee (Product)

Summary (auto): Discovery on data residency, encryption/KMS, logging retention and redaction controls. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options for regulated banking workloads.

[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros—I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, this is Samira and Jordan on the engineering side. How are you all?

[00:10] Tom Richards: Hi Alex, thanks. Tom here, CISO at CopperValley. We brought Nina and Raj.

[00:15] Nina Gomez: Afternoon. We're mostly concerned about where data lives, auditability, and whether we can keep logs out of vendor systems.

[00:25] Alex Moreno: Totally. Today's goal is to understand your compliance reqs (GDPR, HIPAA, banking regs), what data you'd send to models, and surface options—hosted, dedicated, private—and tradeoffs.

[00:35] Samira Patel: Quick note—I'll talk a bit about runtime and what we can lock down at infra level, and Jordan will cover encryption and logging.

[01:10] Raj Banerjee: High level, we're looking at using LLMs for conversational support (customer chat), fraud triage, and internal document routing. Some of the prompts will include account numbers and transaction metadata. So we need controls.

[01:35] Jordan Lee: Understood. First Q: are there any hard prohibitions—like absolutely no data may leave EU, or no third-party storage?

[01:45] Tom Richards: For certain cohorts yes. EU customers' PII must remain in-region for GDPR. Also for a subset of customers that opt-in we need data to never leave our VPC and no vendor-managed logging.

[02:05] Alex Moreno: Great, that's why people often consider Dedicated or Private for those cases. Hosted can be configured for region-restricted hosting, but Dedicated gives reserved capacity and better isolation; Private gives you control of the control plane + on-prem if needed.

[02:28] Nina Gomez: Can you run through the exact differences for logging and audit? Specifically, can we disable request/response logging on hosted?

[02:40] Samira Patel: On our Hosted API we persist operational logs for a short retention for billing and SLOs, but we offer options: customers can enable request-level redaction, configure retention windows, and we support customer-managed KMS for encrypting at rest. For the strictest cases, Dedicated isolates the GPU pool and you can opt out of storing full transcripts—only metrics.

[03:05] Tom Richards: When you say "opt out of storing full transcripts" does that mean logs never leave our environment? Or they still go to Redwood logs but redacted?

[03:15] Jordan Lee: In Dedicated deployments, logs are still collected by the Redwood control plane unless you're on Private. However, we can redact or hash sensitive fields at the API gateway before persisting. Private deployments (VPC/private cloud or on-prem) give you full control: you run the control plane in your environment and logs never go to Redwood-managed tenants.

[03:40] Raj Banerjee: Okay. What's the lift for Private? We're a mid-size bank—on-prem might be heavy.

[03:50] Samira Patel: Private is more ops-heavy—requires network connectivity for licensing and some initial onboarding. We have a VPC-hosted private option where the control plane runs in your cloud account; that reduces on-prem burden. It typically takes a few weeks to onboard plus security review.

[04:10] Nina Gomez: What about HIPAA? If we handle health-like PII for a specific vertical, can Redwood be HIPAA-compatible?

[04:20] Alex Moreno: Short answer: yes, we support HIPAA workflows. We sign a BAA for qualified plans and use encryption in transit and at rest. For PHI we strongly recommend Dedicated or Private, with customer-managed KMS and restricted logging.

[04:40] Tom Richards: We need to know specifics—key rotation, KMS support (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK), HSM integration?

[04:50] Jordan Lee: We support AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and have HSM integrations for higher tiers. Key rotation policies are driven by the customer's KMS—Redwood doesn't manage your keys if you enable CMK. For Hosted customers who don't bring KMS, keys are managed but can be rotated per our policy and audited.

[05:15] Raj Banerjee: Are the model weights stored anywhere outside region? If we pin a model version, could the weights be replicated to another region for redundancy?

[05:25] Samira Patel: By default we replicate for high availability but can restrict replication to specific regions for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we have multi-region failover but can provide region pinning for compliance-sensitive customers.

[05:45] Tom Richards: On audit logs—do you capture user level, token usage, and full request/response? We need tamper-evident logs for SOC2-like audits.

[05:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, we generate audit logs that include API key identity, route, model version, latency, and request IDs. Full request/response capture is optional; for tamper-evident storage we can integrate with your logging pipeline (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK) and ship logs to your S3/GCS bucket with Object Lock (write once) if needed.

[06:20] Nina Gomez: Shipping logs to our bucket is interesting. Are there options to avoid sensitive payloads being sent, like scrub/partial redaction before export?

[06:30] Samira Patel: Absolutely—scrubbing/redaction rules can be applied inline. We have regex-based and schema-based redaction. It's not perfect (transcription issues), but combined with client-side obfuscation you can remove account numbers and replace with tokens before sending.

[06:55] Tom Richards: Can we do client-side tokenization? Like we hash account numbers before sending?

[07:05] Alex Moreno: Yes. Many customers implement a pre-processing layer in their app to tokenize sensitive fields and rehydrate them internally after inference. We can advise on patterns.

[07:20] Raj Banerjee: Latency concern—if we tokenize locally and call Redwood, will that impact throughput? Also question about model variants: hosted has latest models, but dedicated/private might run quantized or different variants—how does quality compare?

[07:40] Samira Patel: There are tradeoffs. Dedicated/Private often run same open model family but can be quantized (int8/4) for cost and performance. We provide quality profiles per quantization; most production prompts see negligible quality drop, but we recommend validation via evals. Latency depends on hardware and batching; tokenization preflight usually adds negligible time if done as part of request pipeline.

[08:15] Tom Richards: For GDPR data residency, we need data residency per-customer—we can't mix storage across tenants. Does Redwood offer per-tenant physical separation?

[08:25] Jordan Lee: Dedicated provides tenant isolation at the compute pool. For Hosted we provide logical separation and region isolation; we can offer tenant-dedicated storage backends for enterprise accounts. Private gives you full physical separation if deployed into your VPC.

[08:45] Nina Gomez: About data subject requests (DSRs) and right to be forgotten—if a user requests deletion, can we ensure propagation across caches, KV caches, and logs?

[08:55] Samira Patel: We support deletion APIs for stored user traces and caches. For KV cache (model key-value), the runtime cache is ephemeral; we can evict and wipe persisted caches. Logs and backups depend on retention and your export policies; if you export logs to your bucket you control deletion. We also maintain deletion workflows for hosted traces on request, subject to audit.

[09:20] Raj Banerjee: Who signs the BAA? Is that standard or needs legal negotiation?

[09:30] Alex Moreno: We have a standard BAA template for enterprise plans. Legal review is typical but it's straightforward—most banks take a few weeks to finalize.

[09:45] Tom Richards: A couple of nitty gritty questions—what about subprocessor lists, and do you have any suppliers that have access to unredacted data?

[09:55] Jordan Lee: We publish a subprocessor list and can provide SOC2 artifact maps that show where data flows. Access to unredacted PII is restricted to rare cases (debugging) and requires customer approval and audit trail.

[10:20] Nina Gomez: Is there a way to disable recording of calls in Fireflies? (laughter) I mean, disable request capture in your system for certain endpoints.

[10:30] Alex Moreno: Ha—no worries. You can disable request-level persistence for specific routes or set retention to zero and stream-only mode, where we never persist the body—only metrics.

[10:45] Tom Richards: For our pilot we want: EU-only residency for EU customers, no plaintext PHI persisted, customer-managed KMS, and audit exports to our logging bucket. Would that be doable on Hosted or do we need Dedicated?

[10:55] Samira Patel: That sounds like a Dedicated profile, but depending on scale we can do Hosted with enterprise controls + tenant-dedicated storage. We should size the pilot and pick the right deployment.

[11:15] Raj Banerjee: Pricing—how do Dedicated costs compare to Hosted? Do you charge for reserved GPUs + software license?

[11:25] Alex Moreno: Dedicated is reserved capacity—monthly commit for GPUs + platform fee. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll send a pricing sheet; for pilot we usually recommend a short-term reserved pool or burstable Dedicated.

[11:40] Tom Richards: Can we bring your runtime into our VPC and still use Redwood console for rollouts?

[11:50] Jordan Lee: Yes, with the VPC-hosted Private option the control plane runs in your account but we provide the console access via a secure management plane. RBAC and SSO integrate with your IdP (SAML/Okta).

[12:10] Nina Gomez: Speaking of SSO, do you support SCIM for user provisioning?

[12:18] Samira Patel: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC; we can map roles to your groups.

[12:30] Raj Banerjee: For the technical deep-dive we'll want to run a small benchmark comparing latency and cost running a T5-like or Llama variant across Hosted vs Dedicated quantized. Can Redwood run that?

[12:40] Alex Moreno: Absolutely. Typical next step: security docs + run a bench. We'll propose a small POC: test three flows (customer chat, fraud triage, doc routing) across model variants and measure latency, tokens, cost and quality.

[13:00] Tom Richards: Ok that sounds good. Who will own the benchmark?

[13:06] Samira Patel: Jordan and I will coordinate with your infra team. We'll need sample prompts and a dataset (anonymized) from you. Ideally small (~500 prompts) to start.

[13:20] Nina Gomez: On retention windows—what's minimum retention for hosted logs?

[13:27] Jordan Lee: We can do as low as 7 days by default for some operational logs; for request bodies you can set retention to zero in enterprise plans or route them to your storage and delete.

[13:45] Tom Richards: Are there export guarantees for logs e.g., delivery retries, ordering, or is it best-effort?

[13:53] Samira Patel: We provide retry semantics and delivery guarantees similar to cloud native exporters; for strict compliance use the direct-to-bucket export which uses S3/GCS APIs with put guarantees and optional Object Lock.

[14:10] Raj Banerjee: A few hypothetical edge cases: 1) model hallucination leaking PII, 2) regulatory subpoenas—what's Redwood's policy?

[14:20] Alex Moreno: For hallucinations you should avoid sending raw PHI and use tokenization. On subpoenas, we follow legal process and will notify customers per our contract and notification policies; if data is only in customer-managed storage we don't have access.

[14:40] Tom Richards: Any customers in banking using your Private option we could reference?

[14:47] Alex Moreno: We can provide references under NDA; several regional banks run Dedicated/Private. I'll get permission and share a reference list.

[15:00] Nina Gomez: Operational question—what's your incident response SLA for security incidents?

[15:10] Jordan Lee: We have incident classification and notification timelines in our SOC2 docs. For enterprise customers we provide a defined playbook and 24/7 on-call contact.

[15:25] Raj Banerjee: About model updates—if Redwood upgrades model weights, can we pin to a specific model version? We can't have silent changes to model behaviour.

[15:35] Samira Patel: Yes—version pinning is standard. We support canary rollouts and A/B testing. We also surface model changes in the console and you can opt into automatic updates.

[15:55] Tom Richards: Anything else we should know about encryption in transit—do you support mTLS?

[16:04] Jordan Lee: We support TLS 1.2/1.3; for Dedicated/Private we support mutual TLS and private endpoints.

[16:20] Alex Moreno: Alright, I want to recap and capture next steps.

[16:28] Alex Moreno: Recap: Customer requirements—EU-only residency for EU customers, no plaintext PHI persisted, customer-managed KMS, audit exports to customer buckets, redaction/tokenization pre-process, and POC for latency/quality. Redwood actions—send SOC2/ISO/BAA templates, provide subprocessor list, propose pilot scope & pricing, schedule infra deep-dive.

[16:55] Tom Richards: That aligns. One ask—can you share a sample ingestion pipeline that shows where to do tokenization and redaction?

[17:05] Samira Patel: Yes we'll include a sample architecture diagram and code snippets in the follow-up.

[17:20] Raj Banerjee: Timing—we're hoping to pilot in Q2. Is that realistic?

[17:30] Alex Moreno: Yes, Q2 pilot is doable if we start now. We'll send paperwork and docs this week.

[17:40] Nina Gomez: Any blockers from our end? We'll need legal approval, infra access for benching, and a dataset.

[17:50] Tom Richards: Ok last question—do you log model prompts for training purposes? Are prompts used to improve your models?

[18:00] Jordan Lee: We do not train on customer data by default. There's an opt-in program for model improvements but enterprise customers can opt-out and we have contractual protections.

[18:15] Alex Moreno: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack.

[18:25] Tom Richards: Thanks—looking forward.

[18:30] (meeting ends)
